paragraphs: Yosef ben Simai: Shabbat 121a. Rosh has Yose; so too Jerusalem Talmud, end of Kol Kitvei, Yoma 8:5, and Nedarim 4:9. A fire broke out in his courtyard at Beit Shean—Jerusalem Talmud: Shichin—on the Sabbath. Men of Sepphoris’s garrison came to extinguish it, because he was the king’s steward, but he did not allow them, out of honor for the Sabbath [ולא הניחוהו as printed; pronoun/subject reading requires collation]. He told them: ‘Let the collector collect his debt.’ Immediately a cloud gathered, rain fell, and extinguished it. Shulchan Arukh, Orach Chayim 334:25: a gentile who comes to extinguish need not be stopped. Yevamot 115a has Abba Yose ben Simai, as does Rif; Rosh has Abba Yosef ben Simai. Two Torah scholars were with him on a ship, and they drowned; Rabbi permitted their wives to marry on women’s testimony. Gilgulei Neshamot writes: Nachshon sanctified Heaven’s name and entered the sea’s surge up to his nose; this Yosef was his reincarnation. Elitzur ben Shedeur, too, entered him through ibbur: he had belonged to Korach’s congregation, which disputed against God, and now, in Yosef, wished to sanctify the Name. At first he sanctified the Name with his body by jumping into the sea; now he wished to sanctify Heaven’s name with his money, allowing his possessions and all his wealth to burn. Just as a miracle was performed for Nachshon and the water came up to his nose, so rain came to save his property. He was also Achan, who profaned the Sabbath because he was eager for wealth; now he sanctified Heaven’s name with his wealth. Nachshon and Achan’s connection was that they were brothers, one from Zerach and one from Peretz, Judah’s sons. This Yosef redeemed them: he rectified the neshamah of one, and the nefesh and ruach of the other. Joshua’s killing of Achan was an emergency ruling, for there were no witnesses or warning. End quotation, letter aleph.
